title: I'm with Him
summary: Job longed for someone to stand between God and man. At the gates of heaven, our only plea is Christ: "I'm with him."
exhortation: Job diagnosed the problem rightly. Who could stand between God and man and bridge that gap?

As a young man I heard a sermon by C.J. Mahaney called "Christ Our Mediator." He told a story about going to his favorite team's baseball stadium. Normally you can't just walk in the entrance the players and important people use. There are guards and a steel door. As he approached, they gave him the side-eye: you don't belong here. But he was with a friend who was recognized and had the badge and the authority. He said, "I'm with him," and walked right in. And the further they went, the more access he was given. The locker room? "I'm with him." The dugout? "I'm with him." Onto the field? "I'm with him."

When we approach the gates of heaven, if what's on our lips is, "Lord, didn't we cast out demons in your name? Didn't we do mighty works? Didn't we plant churches and go to church every Sunday?", that plea will not be enough. The only plea is a humble, repentant heart that says, "I claim nothing but the blood of Christ." He alone can lay his hand on both God and man. So as we sing, let's remember Christ our mediator, whose blood was poured out for the forgiveness of our sins, bridging the gap.
prayer: Lord, we are so grateful that you came and gave us access to the Father through your incarnation, your perfect life, your death on the cross and your resurrection. We can be restored to relationship with you because we are in Christ. Because we are with Christ, we have that access now.

I pray for anyone today who looks at their life and is discouraged, who looks at their past and fears rejection or doubts your acceptance. Lift their eyes to see Jesus, so that they say, "I'm with him." Let them not look to their own works to get in, or to their own sins and faults as a reason to stay away, but to you, Jesus. Lord, do that for them. In Jesus' name, amen.
